—Overall research state

LTC price with moving averages

Daily close, MA30 and MA200. Use the range control to change the window.

Drawdown from ATH close

Maximum daily close in the dataset — not the intraday all-time high.

Raw volume

Volume is kept as a raw field; the unit is not confirmed by the source.

Read: price is below MA200, drawdown from the 2021 close high remains extreme, and 30-observation annualized volatility is high. This is a research snapshot, not a trading signal.

Network activity

Active addresses and transactions. Addresses are a proxy, not unique users.

Hashrate

Coin Metrics units. Hashrate is a security proxy, not a full attack-cost model.

Fees vs issuance

USD values derived from native units × Coin Metrics PriceUSD.

Supply

Visible LTC supply. The hard cap is 84,000,000 LTC.

MVRV

Coin Metrics provider metric. A low value is not a standalone buy signal.

Read: activity is mixed — active addresses and transactions are weaker over 30 days, while hashrate is higher. Fees remain small relative to issuance, so the security budget is still dominated by the block subsidy.

Hashrate and difficulty

Hashrate uses Coin Metrics units; difficulty is the daily average from Blockchair.

Miner revenue composition

Gross miner revenue = subsidy + fees. This is revenue, not profit.

Fee share of miner revenue

A low fee share means the security budget depends on issuance.

Supply and remaining supply

Remaining supply to the 84M cap. Estimates do not model future halving dates.

Read: miner revenue is gross revenue before electricity, capex, pool fees and hedging. Miner cost is not observable from the public data used here, so do not present this as miner profitability.

Market cap vs realized cap

Realized cap is derived as market cap / MVRV.

Peer market cap

Latest common date: —. LTC is highlighted.

Peer comparison table

Different assets, different units. Compare market cap, activity and hashrate together, not one metric alone.

Read: LTC trades at a low MVRV relative to its own history, but MVRV is a provider metric and a low reading is not a standalone buy signal. Peer comparison is descriptive, not a ranking.

Rolling 30-observation annualized volatility

Stdev of daily returns × sqrt(365). Crypto uses 365 periods per year.

Yearly returns

First close to last close within each calendar year.

Monthly return heatmap

Calendar-month return. Partial months are marked in the tooltip.

Yearly risk table

Return, realized volatility and maximum drawdown within each year.

Read: the asset has a long history of large drawdowns and high volatility. VaR is historical and empirical, not a forecast of the maximum possible loss.

Framework: CONFIRMATION requires at least 3 PASS gates and no hard FAIL. CAUTION is a mixed picture. DEFENSIVE is 2 or more hard FAILs. This is a pre-trade review framework, not a personalized recommendation or a substitute for position limits.

Data quality checks

Known limitations are part of the research output, not an afterthought.

Sources

Provider, coverage, terms and known limitations.

Reproduce: market data from the uploaded LTC file; on-chain, supply and peer data from Coin Metrics Community API v4; block-level aggregates from Blockchair. Review provider terms before commercial use. The dashboard is a research snapshot, not investment advice.
